# Anivora 0.1.34 — Online Cast and QR TV pairing

- Add Google Cast to eligible online Android episode streams using Google's Default Media Receiver. Choose a device on the same Wi-Fi network, view its name, and control play/pause, seeking, stopping and disconnecting from the phone. Leaving the player or changing the episode/source ends the Cast session.
- Add Profile → TV pairing with camera QR scanning, explicit confirmation, sign-in continuation and manual code entry when the camera is unavailable. QR payloads are restricted to Anivora's pairing links.
- Add durable MongoDB pairing APIs for a future TV client: create a ten-minute code, complete it once using a verified phone account, securely poll with an independent session secret, and unlink the session. The TV-side contract is documented; no Android TV application is included.
- Preserve the existing signed GitHub APK updater, Cloudflare pages, remote avatar catalog and small offline fallback set, direct on-device manga providers, server-status notices and native download/HLS engine. Media, manga image, avatar and APK bytes are not routed through Render for these features.

Android version code: **36**, newer than 0.1.33/code 35. Package:
`com.brandon300.anivora`. ARM64, Android 7.0/API 24 or newer. Retains the existing
signing certificate so this APK can install over the existing app without uninstalling.

## Limitations

- Cast supports online public HTTPS HLS/DASH/MP4 sources that the receiver can fetch directly. Downloaded/local files, embedded provider pages and streams needing phone-only headers/cookies are not castable. Providers may still reject receiver requests or expire a URL; Anivora shows a recoverable error.
- TV pairing requires a future compatible TV client and a running API/database. The owner's Anivora1 Render service was billing-suspended at release preparation, so live pairing remains unavailable until that service is restored. A phone update cannot clear a hosting billing suspension.
- Physical Chromecast, Android TV, phone-camera and Infinix Hot 50i certification are not claimed. Automated/native validation and emulator checks are separate from real-device interoperability.

The release pipeline verifies TypeScript/lint, app and backend tests, Expo
compatibility, native unit regressions, Android 14 download/HLS integration,
release package/version/signature, compiled source, Cast/camera native packaging,
and the six bundled avatar fallbacks before publication. Public APK downloads are
checksum-verified before the updater feed changes. The build attaches its exact
source commit and SHA-256 checksum to the release.

See [Cast details](casting.md), the [phone/API TV pairing contract](tv-pairing.md),
and the [0.1.33 release snapshot](releases/0.1.33.md).
